messages.content: Draft an HHVC Transaction page for bed bug complaints. Use this exact heading format: PAGE NAME:, PAGE TYPE:, PRIMARY USER:. Include clear next steps and mention 311.

judgeSamples.output:
# Bed Bug Complaint Draft — Karl CMS

---

## PAGE NAME: Report a Bed Bug Problem

## PAGE TYPE: Transaction

## PRIMARY USER: Renter, tenant, or building resident who has discovered bed bugs and needs to file a complaint with the City

---

## What This Page Does

This is a **Transaction page** because it is the entry point into a City service — the resident must *do something* (file a complaint) with a City department. It is not purely informational.

> Per the Karl editor guide on choosing a content type: a Transaction page must be actionable and serve as the entry-point into a service.
> 📎 https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/choosing-a-content-type

---

## DRAFT PAGE CONTENT

---

### Report a Bed Bug Problem

If you have bed bugs in your home or building, you can file a complaint with the City. San Francisco's Department of Public Health (SFDPH) investigates bed bug complaints in residential buildings.

**You can report a bed bug problem if you:**
- Live in a rental unit, residential hotel, or multi-unit building
- Have seen bed bugs or have bites you believe are from bed bugs
- Believe your landlord has not addressed the problem

---

### How to file a complaint

**Online or by phone — contact 311**

The fastest way to report a bed bug problem is through **SF 311**, the City's customer service center.

- 📞 **Call 311** (or 415-701-2311 from outside SF)
- 💻 **File online at sf311.org**
- 📱 **Use the SF311 app** on iPhone or Android

311 will route your complaint to the San Francisco Department of Public Health for follow-up.

---

### What happens next

1. **Your complaint is received** — 311 logs your complaint and sends it to SFDPH.
2. **An inspector is assigned** — SFDPH will review your complaint and may schedule an inspection of your unit or building.
3. **Inspection takes place** — An inspector visits to confirm the infestation and document conditions.
4. **Notice is issued to your landlord** — If bed bugs are confirmed, SFDPH may issue a notice of violation requiring the landlord to arrange treatment.
5. **Follow-up** — SFDPH may re-inspect to confirm the problem has been addressed.

⏱ *Response times vary. For urgent health concerns, call 311 directly.*

---

### Before you file

It helps to have this information ready:
- Your full address, including unit number
- Your name and a contact phone number or email
- A description of what you've seen (live bugs, shells, bites, staining)
- Dates when you first noticed the problem
- Whether you have already notified your landlord

---

## SUPPORTING INFORMATION SECTIONS

> These sections appear below the main flow on the live page. Custom headings are yours to set — the default "Supporting information" label does **not** display publicly.
> 📎 https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/building-a-page-by-content-type/transaction/supporting-information-on-a-transaction-page

---

### Your rights as a tenant

San Francisco landlords are required to maintain rental units free of pests, including bed bugs, under the San Francisco Housing Code. Landlords must respond promptly to reports of infestation and arrange licensed pest control treatment.

If your landlord is not responding, you may also contact the **Rent Board** or seek advice from a **tenant rights organization** such as the Tenderloin Housing Clinic or Causa Justa.

---

### What landlords are required to do

Landlords in San Francisco must:
- Respond to tenant complaints about bed bugs
- Hire a licensed pest control operator for treatment
- Not retaliate against tenants for filing complaints with the City

---

### Bed bug prevention tips

- Inspect secondhand furniture before bringing it inside
- Use mattress encasements rated for bed bug protection
- Reduce clutter where bed bugs can hide
- Report signs of infestation to your landlord in writing as soon as possible

---

## RELATED PAGES

> Only Transaction, Information, Campaign, and Topic pages can be added as Related. Titles and descriptions sync automatically when the linked page is updated.
> 📎 https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/components/related

Suggested Related pages (right rail):
- **Report a Housing Code Violation** *(Transaction)*
- **Tenant Rights in San Francisco** *(Information)*
- **Contact Your Landlord About Repairs** *(Information)*
- **SF Rent Board** *(Transaction or Topic)*

---

## EDITOR NOTES

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Page type | Transaction |
| Department | San Francisco Department of Public Health (SFDPH) |
| Service owner | HHVC (Housing & Health Code Violations team) |
| 311 routing | Yes — primary intake channel |
| Requires login | No |
| Related pages linked | Transaction + Information only (per Karl rules) |

---

*Draft prepared for HHVC review. Content should be verified against current SFDPH complaint intake procedures before publishing.*

messages.content: Create an HHVC Information page about mold prevention for tenants. Keep language simple, and preserve headings PAGE NAME:, PAGE TYPE:, PRIMARY USER:.

judgeSamples.output:
Here is the draft Information page for Karl CMS:

---

**PAGE NAME:** Prevent mold in your rental home

**PAGE TYPE:** Information
*(Not actionable — no City transaction required. If tenants need to report mold, link that via a Transaction page using the Part of component. See:* https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/building-a-page-by-content-type/information/part-of-on-an-information-page*)*

**PRIMARY USER:** Residential tenants in San Francisco

---

## Page description (internal summary)

Tips to help tenants stop mold from growing in their rental home.

---

## What you need to know

Mold grows when moisture builds up indoors. As a tenant, you can take simple steps to keep your home dry and reduce the chance of mold forming.

---

## Keep air moving

* Open windows when you cook, shower, or do laundry.
* Use the bathroom fan every time you shower or bathe.
* Leave cabinet doors open under sinks so air can circulate.
* Move furniture a few inches away from walls so air flows behind it.

---

## Reduce moisture at home

* Wipe down wet surfaces in the bathroom and kitchen after use.
* Fix dripping faucets as soon as you notice them.
* Dry wet clothes and towels fully before folding or storing them.
* Do not hang wet laundry indoors if you can avoid it.
* Empty drip trays under plants and refrigerators regularly.

---

## Control humidity

* Keep indoor humidity below 50% if possible.
* Use a dehumidifier in rooms that feel damp.
* Do not block vents or air returns with furniture or boxes.

---

## Check for early signs of mold

Look for:

* Dark spots or staining on walls, ceilings, or grout
* A musty or earthy smell
* Peeling paint or wallpaper
* Condensation on windows or pipes

If you see or smell mold, act quickly. Small patches can grow fast.

---

## What to do if you find mold

**Small areas (roughly the size of a piece of paper or smaller):**
You may be able to clean it yourself using soap and water or a diluted bleach solution. Wear gloves and open windows while you clean.

**Larger areas or mold that keeps coming back:**
Tell your landlord in writing right away. Landlords in San Francisco are required to keep rental units safe and habitable. Ongoing or widespread mold may be their responsibility to fix.

---

## Tell your landlord

* Report moisture problems and mold in writing — email or text works.
* Keep a copy of what you sent.
* Take photos with the date visible.

Keeping a record protects you if the problem is not fixed.

---

## Get more help

If your landlord does not respond, you can contact the San Francisco Department of Building Inspection or the Rent Board for guidance.

*(Link to relevant Transaction pages for reporting or filing a complaint here, using the Related component — only Transaction, Information, Campaign, and Topic pages can be tagged as Related:* https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/components/related*)*

---

### Editor notes (not published)

* Tag this page to the appropriate Transaction page using **Part of** so it appears in context.
* Add Related pages for reporting housing violations or contacting the Rent Board.
* Review with HHVC subject matter expert before publishing.
* Plain language level: aim for 6th–8th grade reading level.

output.summary: Transaction type is correct and 311 is referenced, but the page lacks actionable first-person language, uses hidden verbs and passive voice, omits tenant responsibilities, and is missing Related pages and supporting information sections required by Karl Transaction standards.
passed: Page type is valid Karl content type: Transaction
All components used are from valid Karl list: Title, Description, What to know, What to do
311 reference present in What to do section
System Relationships correctly lists parent as Topic
warnings: Title is not action-oriented or in first person — change 'Report bed bugs in your apartment' to 'Report bed bugs in my apartment' or 'Report a bed bug problem'
What to know section leads with background rather than user benefit — lead with 'You should report bed bugs quickly' instead of 'Bed bugs spread quickly'
Paragraph length: What to know section contains 2 sentences but lacks connection to user action

Missing Related pages component — per https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/building-a-page-by-content-type/transaction, Transaction pages should include Related pages on the right for supporting content

Missing Supporting information section — per https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/building-a-page-by-content-type/transaction/supporting-information-on-a-transaction-page, Transaction pages should include extra sections below the main flow for additional text with custom headings
Tenant responsibilities not included — specify what tenant must do before/after inspection (e.g., prepare unit, document infestation)
failed: Hidden verbs detected: 'conduct an inspection' (in What to know) — use active verb 'inspect' or 'we inspect' instead
Hidden verb: 'file a complaint' (in What to do) — rewrite as 'call 311 to report' or 'call 311 to complain'
Passive voice: 'We inspect for signs of infestation' — rewrite as active construction 'We look for signs of infestation' or 'We check your home for bed bug signs'
Reader not consistently addressed as 'you' — What to know and What to do sections use 'we' instead of 'you'; rewrite to 'You should keep records' and 'You can call 311'
Description does not use 'you' — rewrite to 'Call 311 to report a bed bug problem so we can inspect your home' to address reader directly

judgeSamples.output:
PAGE NAME: Fix trash and pest problems in shared buildings
PAGE TYPE: Transaction
PRIMARY USER: Property owner

SECTION: What you need to do
If a tenant reports a trash or pest problem, you must respond and fix it. Call 311 to get city support.

**Action Link:** Call 311

SECTION: What we inspect
We inspect shared areas in buildings for trash buildup and pest activity. This includes hallways, trash rooms, and common outdoor areas. Inspections follow SF Health Code Article 11.

**Callout:** DPH inspects health and cleanliness issues like trash and pests. DBI handles structural and safety issues like broken stairs or walls. If you are not sure who to call, start with 311.

SECTION: Owner responsibilities
As the owner, you must:
- Respond to tenant complaints about trash or pests quickly
- Set up and pay for trash pickup
- Fix pest problems by hiring a pest control service
- Keep all shared areas clean and free of pests

**Callout — Sewage or bed bugs:** If the problem involves sewage or bed bugs, the city treats this as urgent. You must expect an inspector within 48 hours.

SECTION: Tenant and owner responsibilities
Owners are responsible for shared spaces. Tenants are responsible for keeping their own unit clean. Both must work together when a problem is reported.

SECTION: Contact
Call 311 to report a problem or ask for help. You can also visit the DPH office in person.

**Action Link:** Call 311

---

DUPLICATION RISKS:
- This page may overlap with existing SF.gov pages on 311 service requests or DBI permit complaints. Confirm with the web team before publishing.
